newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE STARTS AS RELUCTANT FAVOURITE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE STARTS AS RELUCTANT FAVOURITE.

text.p: At the relatively tender age of 25, Jacques Villeneuve is already installed as one of the hottest, and most reluctant, favourites in years to win the Formula One drivers' world championship.

The Candian son of the legendary Ferrari driver Gilles Villeneuve, who was killed in 1982, has stepped into the Williams' lead driver's position vacated by defending world champion Damon Hill of Britain.
But, instead of easing into the role, he has been doing his best to play down his chances of taking the title.
"It would be great to feel like the favourite for the championship and I'm looking forward to being up there," said Villeneuve, who finished runner-up last year.
"But you never know what's going to happen. A lot of people say it is already finished -- and that's dangerous.
"It's my plan to win the title. I'm very excited about it and I hope it goes well. That's the reason you're racing -- to be competitive, to win, and to fight for the championship."
Where his father Gilles was romanticised by his fans for his cavalier outlook on life and racing, Jacques has instead developed a far more practical attitude to both -- he simply races to win.
Former three-times world champion Jackie Stewart, who is launching his own team this season, believes that Villeneuve's failure to win the title last autumn will work to his advantage this year.
"Gilles was the ultimate seat of the pants driver. His car control was superb. He would get cars at incredible angles. The fans loved it. But the bank manager probably didn't.

"Jacques is different. He would never try to drive a car back to the pits on two wheels, for example. He's a considerably more advanced version of Gilles -- he has far better mind management. And that's vital to a driver.

"I loved his father. He was a 10/10ths driver. And sometimes an 11/10ths driver. But, some days, you have got to drive slowly....How many races has Jacques won, versus his father? Four against six. He's nearly eclipsed his father already. I'm not having a go at Gilles. I'm just being realistic."

Jacques Villeneuve is just as realistic. He knows that after a winter spent relaxing at his home in Monte Carlo and skiing, before the resumption of pre-season testing, he has to fulfill all expectations this time.
"I know everything now, there is nothing for me to learn. I just have to adapt a bit and improve what I've learnt so far -- the mentality, the drivers and all that and F1 in general.

"But knowing the tracks will help a lot because I'll be able to work on the set-up of the car with Jock (Clear, his race engineer) right from the very first laps and without being pushed to use a Damon-based set-up like we were last year until halfway through the season.

"That's what hurt the most. Our set-ups weren't really compatible but towards the end of the season the base set-up was closer to mine. So, for the first half of the season, it was difficult for me to get the most out of the car."

With Villeneuve, all conversations about racing revolve around performance and competition and are conducted in an analytical and straightforward way. Even the pressures he is under as favourite are treated in the same manner.

"This kind of pressure is more positive than last year," he said. "Last year, a lot of the pressure was people expecting me to fall on my face and you have to prove them wrong. Now people are expecting me to perform, so you have to prove them right. It's an easier pressure."
He admitted he is more excited this year than last. "There is only one way to go -- to try and win. I'm confident in the team and the car and all the things I learned are going to be useful."

Villeneuve, however, understands that winning the title may not be an easy task. "You're always satisfied when you win, and you often end up saying second is the first of the losers," he said. "But it depends on the situation.

"You can't judge in advance if you'll be disappointed if you don't win because it depends on what happens during the season. I'll be disappointed if I don't do the best I can with what I've got in my hands or in a given situation.
"But if the best we can do is not win, because something else happens....then you have to accept it."
